title: The hidden network that makes the internet possible - Sajan Saini

blocks.en_text: a team of Japanese and Danish researchers set a world record,
blocks.zh_text: 一个由日本和丹麦研究人员组成的团队创下了一项世界纪录，

blocks.en_text: transmitting 1 petabit of data—
blocks.zh_text: 在一秒内传输了1拍比特的数据——

blocks.en_text: that’s 10,000 hours of high-def video—
blocks.zh_text: 相当于1万小时的高清视频——

blocks.en_text: over a fifty-kilometer cable, in a second.
blocks.zh_text: 通过一条五十公里长的光缆。

blocks.en_text: This wasn’t just any cable.
blocks.zh_text: 这可不是普通的光缆。

blocks.en_text: It was a souped-up version of fiber optics—
blocks.zh_text: 它是光纤的升级加强版——

blocks.en_text: the hidden network that links our planet
blocks.zh_text: 这个隐藏的网络连接着我们的星球，

blocks.en_text: and makes the internet possible.
blocks.zh_text: 让互联网成为可能。

blocks.en_text: For decades,
blocks.zh_text: 几十年来，

blocks.en_text: long-distance communications between cities and countries
blocks.zh_text: 城市与国家之间的长途通信

blocks.en_text: were carried by electrical signals,
blocks.zh_text: 都是靠电信号传输的，

blocks.en_text: in wires made of copper.
blocks.zh_text: 用的是铜制的导线。

blocks.en_text: This was slow and inefficient,
blocks.zh_text: 这种方式又慢又低效，

blocks.en_text: with metal wires limiting data rates and power lost as wasted heat.
blocks.zh_text: 金属导线限制了数据传输速率，电能还以废热的形式白白损耗。

blocks.en_text: But in the late 20th century,
blocks.zh_text: 但在20世纪末，

blocks.en_text: engineers mastered a far superior method of transmission.
blocks.zh_text: 工程师们掌握了一种优越得多的传输方式。

blocks.en_text: Instead of metal,
blocks.zh_text: 不用金属，

blocks.en_text: glass can be carefully melted and drawn into flexible fiber strands,
blocks.zh_text: 而是把玻璃小心地熔化、拉制成柔韧的纤维丝，

blocks.en_text: hundreds of kilometers long and no thicker than human hair.
blocks.zh_text: 长达数百公里，却比人的头发还细。

blocks.en_text: And instead of electricity,
blocks.zh_text: 而且不用电，

blocks.en_text: these strands carry pulses of light, representing digital data.
blocks.zh_text: 这些纤维丝传输的是光脉冲，用来表示数字数据。

blocks.en_text: But how does light travel within glass, rather than just pass through it?
blocks.zh_text: 可是，光如何在玻璃内部传播，而不是直接穿过去呢？

blocks.en_text: The trick lies in a phenomenon known as total internal reflection.
blocks.zh_text: 诀窍在于一种叫做全反射的现象。

blocks.en_text: Since Isaac Newton’s time,
blocks.zh_text: 自艾萨克·牛顿时代起，

blocks.en_text: lensmakers and scientists have known that light bends
blocks.zh_text: 镜片制造商和科学家就知道，光会发生弯折，

blocks.en_text: when it passes between air and materials like water or glass.
blocks.zh_text: 当它在空气和水或玻璃这类材料之间穿过时。

blocks.en_text: When a ray of light inside glass hits its surface at a steep angle,
blocks.zh_text: 当玻璃内部的一束光以陡峭的角度射到表面时，

blocks.en_text: it refracts, or bends as it exits into air.
blocks.zh_text: 它会折射，也就是在射入空气时发生弯折。

blocks.en_text: But if the ray travels at a shallow angle,
blocks.zh_text: 但如果这束光以很浅的角度传播，

blocks.en_text: it’ll bend so far that it stays trapped,
blocks.zh_text: 它就会弯折得太多，以至于被困住，

blocks.en_text: bouncing along inside the glass.
blocks.zh_text: 在玻璃内部不断反射前行。

blocks.en_text: Under the right condition,
blocks.zh_text: 在合适的条件下，

blocks.en_text: something normally transparent to light can instead hide it from the world.
blocks.zh_text: 原本对光透明的物质，反而能把光藏起来，不让外界看到。

blocks.en_text: Compared to electricity or radio,
blocks.zh_text: 与电或无线电相比，

blocks.en_text: fiber optic signals barely degrade over great distances—
blocks.zh_text: 光纤信号在长距离传输中几乎不会衰减——

blocks.en_text: a little power does scatter away,
blocks.zh_text: 会有一点点能量散射掉，

blocks.en_text: and fibers can’t bend too sharply,
blocks.zh_text: 而且光纤不能弯得太急，

blocks.en_text: otherwise the light leaks out.
blocks.zh_text: 否则光就会泄漏出去。

blocks.en_text: Today, a single optical fiber carries many wavelengths of light,
blocks.zh_text: 如今，一根光纤可以承载许多种波长的光，

blocks.en_text: each a different channel of data.
blocks.zh_text: 每一种波长都是一个独立的数据通道。

blocks.en_text: And a fiber optic cable contains hundreds of these fiber strands.
blocks.zh_text: 而一根光缆里包含数百根这样的纤维丝。

blocks.en_text: Over a million kilometers of cable crisscross our ocean floors
blocks.zh_text: 超过一百万公里的光缆纵横交错于我们的海底，

blocks.en_text: to link the continents—
blocks.zh_text: 把各个大洲连接起来——

blocks.en_text: that’s enough to wind around the Equator nearly thirty times.
blocks.zh_text: 这长度足以绕赤道将近三十圈。

blocks.en_text: With fiber optics,
blocks.zh_text: 有了光纤，

blocks.en_text: distance hardly limits data,
blocks.zh_text: 距离几乎不再限制数据，

blocks.en_text: which has allowed the internet to evolve into a planetary computer.
blocks.zh_text: 这让互联网得以发展成一台行星级的计算机。

blocks.en_text: Increasingly,
blocks.zh_text: 越来越多地，

blocks.en_text: our mobile work and play rely on legions of overworked computer servers,
blocks.zh_text: 我们移动办公和娱乐都依赖于大批超负荷运转的计算机服务器，

blocks.en_text: warehoused in gigantic data centers flung across the world.
blocks.zh_text: 它们被安置在世界各地庞大的数据中心里。

blocks.en_text: This is called cloud computing,
blocks.zh_text: 这就叫做云计算。

blocks.en_text: and it leads to two big problems:
blocks.zh_text: 这带来了两大问题：

blocks.en_text: heat waste and bandwidth demand.
blocks.zh_text: 热量浪费和带宽需求。

blocks.en_text: The vast majority of internet traffic shuttles around inside data centers,
blocks.zh_text: 绝大多数互联网流量都在数据中心内部来回传输，

blocks.en_text: where thousands of servers are connected by traditional electrical cables.
blocks.zh_text: 那里成千上万台服务器由传统的电缆连接。

blocks.en_text: Half of their running power is wasted as heat.
blocks.zh_text: 它们运行所耗电力有一半以热量形式浪费掉了。

blocks.en_text: Meanwhile, wireless bandwidth demand steadily marches on,
blocks.zh_text: 与此同时，无线带宽需求稳步增长，

blocks.en_text: and the gigahertz signals used in our mobile devices
blocks.zh_text: 而我们移动设备中使用的千兆赫兹信号

blocks.en_text: are reaching their data delivery limits.
blocks.zh_text: 正逐渐达到其数据传输的极限。

blocks.en_text: It seems fiber optics has been too good for its own good,
blocks.zh_text: 看来光纤技术好得过了头，反而给自己带来了麻烦，

blocks.en_text: fueling overly-ambitious cloud and mobile computing expectations.
blocks.zh_text: 助长了对云计算和移动计算过于雄心勃勃的期待。

blocks.en_text: But a related technology, integrated photonics, has come to the rescue.
blocks.zh_text: 但一项相关的技术——集成光子学——来救场了。

blocks.en_text: Light can be guided not only in optical fibers,
blocks.zh_text: 光不仅可以在光纤中传导，

blocks.en_text: but also in ultrathin silicon wires.
blocks.zh_text: 也可以在超细的硅线中传导。

blocks.en_text: Silicon wires don’t guide light as well as fiber.
blocks.zh_text: 硅线导光的效果不如光纤。

blocks.en_text: But they do enable engineers to shrink
blocks.zh_text: 但它们确实能让工程师把

blocks.en_text: all the devices in a hundred kilometer fiber optic network
blocks.zh_text: 一个百公里光纤网络中的所有器件

blocks.en_text: down to tiny photonic chips that plug into servers
blocks.zh_text: 缩小成微小的光子芯片，插进服务器里，

blocks.en_text: and convert their electrical signals to optical and back.
blocks.zh_text: 把它们的电信号转换成光信号，再转换回来。

blocks.en_text: These electricity-to-light chips allow for wasteful electrical cables in data centers
blocks.zh_text: 这些电光转换芯片让数据中心里浪费电的电缆

blocks.en_text: to be swapped out for power-efficient fiber.
blocks.zh_text: 可以被节能的光纤所取代。

blocks.en_text: Photonic chips can help break open wireless bandwidth limitations, too.
blocks.zh_text: 光子芯片也有助于打破无线带宽的限制。

blocks.en_text: Researchers are working to replace mobile gigahertz signals
blocks.zh_text: 研究人员正致力于用太赫兹频率

blocks.en_text: with terahertz frequencies,
blocks.zh_text: 取代移动设备的千兆赫兹信号，

blocks.en_text: to carry data thousands of times faster.
blocks.zh_text: 从而以快上数千倍的速度传输数据。

blocks.en_text: But these are short-range signals:
blocks.zh_text: 但这些是短距离信号：

blocks.en_text: they get absorbed by moisture in the air,
blocks.zh_text: 它们会被空气中的水分吸收，

blocks.en_text: or blocked by tall buildings.
blocks.zh_text: 或者被高楼挡住。

blocks.en_text: With tiny wireless-to-fiber photonic transmitter chips
blocks.zh_text: 借助微小的无线转光纤光子发射芯片，

blocks.en_text: distributed throughout cities,
blocks.zh_text: 把它们分布到城市各处，

blocks.en_text: terahertz signals can be relayed over long-range distances.
blocks.zh_text: 太赫兹信号就能中继传输到很远的地方。

blocks.en_text: They can do so via a stable middleman,
blocks.zh_text: 它们可以通过一个稳定的中间媒介做到这一点，

blocks.en_text: optical fiber, and make hyperfast wireless connectivity a reality.
blocks.zh_text: 那就是光纤，从而让超高速无线连接成为现实。

blocks.en_text: For all of human history,
blocks.zh_text: 在整个人类历史上，

blocks.en_text: light has gifted us with sight and heat,
blocks.zh_text: 光一直赐予我们视觉和温暖，

blocks.en_text: serving as a steady companion while we explored and settled the physical world.
blocks.zh_text: 在我们探索和定居于物质世界的过程中，始终如一地陪伴着我们。

blocks.en_text: Now, we’ve saddled light with information and redirected it
blocks.zh_text: 如今，我们让光承载信息，并引导它

blocks.en_text: to run along a fiber optic superhighway—
blocks.zh_text: 沿着光纤高速公路奔跑——

blocks.en_text: with many different integrated photonic exits—
blocks.zh_text: 沿途有许多不同的集成光子出口——

blocks.en_text: to build an even more expansive, virtual world.
blocks.zh_text: 去构建一个更加广阔的虚拟世界。
